commands.name: batch:cancel
commands.description: Cancel the workflows a visibility query selects, with a resumable manifest
commands.synopsis: batch:cancel [-s|--server [SERVER]] [--namespace [NAMESPACE]] [--token [TOKEN]] [--tls-verify TLS-VERIFY] [--env ENV] [--output OUTPUT] [--query QUERY] [-t|--type [TYPE]] [--status [STATUS]] [-l|--limit [LIMIT]] [--reason [REASON]] [--manifest MANIFEST] [--rate [RATE]] [-y|--yes] [--json]
commands.help:
Select up to <comment>--limit</comment> workflows with a visibility query, pin each to the run
the listing reported, and record the selection in a new private manifest
before cancelling anything. Each run is cancelled with exactly one request
and its outcome is recorded as it arrives. If the batch stops, resume it
with <comment>dw batch:resume</comment>: targets already done are never sent again, and a
target whose outcome is unknown is reported for inspection, never resent.
See docs/batch-operations.md for the manifest format and recovery steps.

<comment>Examples:</comment>

  <info>dw batch:cancel --query='customer-42' --manifest=cancel-42.jsonl</info>
  <info>dw batch:cancel --query='customer-42' --reason=offboarded --manifest=c.jsonl --yes --json</info>

commands.name: batch:signal
commands.description: Signal the workflows a visibility query selects, with a resumable manifest
commands.synopsis: batch:signal [-s|--server [SERVER]] [--namespace [NAMESPACE]] [--token [TOKEN]] [--tls-verify TLS-VERIFY] [--env ENV] [--output OUTPUT] [--query QUERY] [-t|--type [TYPE]] [--status [STATUS]] [-l|--limit [LIMIT]] [--manifest MANIFEST] [--rate [RATE]] [-y|--yes] [--json] [-i|--input [INPUT]] [--input-file [INPUT-FILE]] [--input-encoding [INPUT-ENCODING]] [--] <signal-name>
commands.help:
Select up to <comment>--limit</comment> workflows with a visibility query, pin each to the run
the listing reported, and record the selection, the signal and its input in
a new private manifest before sending anything. Each target gets its own
command key (<comment>request_id</comment>), reused unchanged on resume. A target whose
outcome is unknown is reported for inspection and never resent: a request ID
alone does not prove a repeated signal is safe.
See docs/batch-operations.md for the manifest format and recovery steps.

<comment>Examples:</comment>

  <info>dw batch:signal approve --query='queue-7' --manifest=approve.jsonl</info>
  <info>dw batch:signal payment_received --query='batch-9' -i '{"amount":10}' --manifest=pay.jsonl --yes</info>

commands.name: batch:resume
commands.description: Continue a batch from its manifest without relisting or resending
commands.help:
Continue the targets of a recorded batch that have no definite outcome:
never dispatched, refused for authentication, or still under Server pressure.
Resume never relists, so it never retargets a successor run, and it reuses
each target's command key. It never resends acknowledged, refused, skipped
or unknown targets. The connection must name the same Server and namespace
the batch recorded.
See docs/batch-operations.md for the manifest format and recovery steps.

<comment>Examples:</comment>

  <info>dw batch:resume cancel-42.jsonl</info>
  <info>dw batch:resume approve.jsonl --yes --json</info>

commands.name: batch:show
commands.description: Show a batch's progress from its manifest, without contacting the Server
commands.help:
Read a batch manifest and print each target's state: acknowledged, skipped,
refused, pressure, unknown or pending. Makes no network requests.
See docs/batch-operations.md for the manifest format and recovery steps.

<comment>Examples:</comment>

  <info>dw batch:show cancel-42.jsonl</info>
  <info>dw batch:show cancel-42.jsonl --json</info>
